title: Do VLMs Reason Like Engineers? A Benchmark and a Stage-wise Evaluation
notes: engineering_web: must-cite - EngVQA (696 multimodal problems in five mechanical-engineering subjects) scores each solution stage with EngJudge, an 8-stage LLM evaluator validated against human grades (Pearson 0.975), so the May claim that engineering benchmarks stop at outcome matching no longer holds.

title: TPS-CalcBench: A Benchmark and Diagnostic Evaluation Framework for LLM Analytical Calculation Competence in Hypersonic Thermal Protection System Engineering
authors: Jinglai Zheng, Chuhan Qiao, Haiming Huang
notes: engineering_web: must-cite - closed-form engineering calculations scored on a dual track (result accuracy plus an 8-dimension reasoning rubric with a calibrated judge and human audit) to catch right-answer-wrong-reasoning; the closest single-domain analogue of EngTrace's process evaluation.

title: Engineering Reasoning and Instruction (ERI) Benchmark: A Large Taxonomy-driven Dataset for Foundation Models and Agents
notes: engineering_web: must-cite - a nine-discipline engineering suite (55 subdomains, 57,750 LLM-generated records) scored by a multi-judge LLM panel on a five-point scale; the broadest direct competitor to EngTrace's cross-branch coverage, and it cites EngTrace, but its reference answers are model-generated rather than code-derived.

title: ThermoQA: A Three-Tier Benchmark for Evaluating Thermodynamic Reasoning in Large Language Models
notes: engineering_web: must-cite - 293 open-ended engineering-thermodynamics problems whose ground truth is computed with CoolProp and whose multi-step tiers are scored step by step on weighted intermediate values; the nearest precedent for EngTrace's code-derived gold and milestone coverage, so the revision must say how milestone coverage differs.

title: CircuChain: Disentangling Competence and Compliance in LLM Circuit Analysis
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - counterbalanced Control/Trap circuit problems verified with symbolic solvers, SPICE and an LLM error taxonomy that attributes failures to convention, physics, arithmetic or hallucination; parallels EngTrace's per-claim arithmetic check and its template-exploitation probes.

title: MechReason: Benchmarking Multi-Image Multi-Hop Reasoning in Mechanical Engineering
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 12k mechanical-engineering QA pairs mined from research papers, with explicit reasoning-chain annotations and shortcut-preventing question generation; new mechanical-branch work (posted Aug/Sep 2026), multimodal, static, and scored on final answers matched by an LLM judge.

title: EngiWorld: What Can Frontier Agents Deliver in Professional Engineering Environments?
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 1,301 expert-curated agent tasks on 26 professional tools (CAD, CAE, CAM, BIM, EDA) with domain verifiers that check final and intermediate artifacts; the strongest new example of the tool-use line the May draft calls tangential (FEABench, EngDesign).

title: StructureClaw: Traceable LLM Agents and an Executable Benchmark for Structural Engineering Workflows
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 150 executable structural-engineering scenarios in which a trial passes only if every required artifact (model, solver responses, checks) matches frozen references; argues, as EngTrace does, that fluent final outputs can hide incomplete or inconsistent work.

title: SoM-1K: A Thousand-Problem Benchmark Dataset for Strength of Materials
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 1,065 annotated strength-of-materials problems (text plus schematics), best model 56.6%; a static, answer-scored mechanical/civil benchmark that exemplifies the sub-discipline silos the Related Work describes.

title: Capabilities of Large Language Models in Control Engineering: A Benchmark Study on GPT-4, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini 1.0 Ultra
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - ControlBench, undergraduate control problems graded by a panel of human experts for accuracy and reasoning, from the same group as the already-cited TransportBench and EngDesign; the standard control-engineering reference.

title: CircuitSense: A Hierarchical MLLM Benchmark Bridging Visual Comprehension and Symbolic Reasoning in Engineering Design Process
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 8,006+ circuit problems from a synthetic schematic and block-diagram generator with auto-derived symbolic equation labels; a generated-instance engineering benchmark to set beside EngTrace's templates (perception above 85%, symbolic derivation below 19%).

title: OPT-Engine: Benchmarking the Limits of LLMs in Optimization Modeling via Complexity Scaling
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - an extensible generator over ten canonical operations-research problems with controllable complexity from LP to MIP; the OR/industrial counterpart of EngTrace's parameterised generation, and it reports chain-of-thought arithmetic failing as complexity grows.

title: SupChain-Bench: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Real-World Supply Chain Management
authors: Shengyue Guan, Yihao Liu, Lang Cao
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - supply-chain knowledge plus long-horizon, SOP-grounded tool orchestration; an ACL-venue industrial-engineering benchmark that the industrial branch of the Related Work should acknowledge.

title: WirelessMathBench: A Mathematical Modeling Benchmark for LLMs in Wireless Communications
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 587 questions from 40 research papers, from multiple choice to full equation completion under physical and dimensional constraints (best model 7.83% on full completion); an ACL-venue communications-engineering benchmark.

title: TeleMath: A Benchmark for Large Language Models in Telecom Mathematical Problem Solving
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - 500 numeric-answer telecom problems (signal processing, network optimisation, performance analysis) expanded from expert-written seed problems by a generation pipeline; a semi-synthetic electrical/communications benchmark scored on final answers only.

title: AstroMind: A High-Fidelity Benchmark for Spacecraft Behavior Reasoning Based on Large Language Models
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - converts high-fidelity astrodynamics simulations into verifiable reasoning problems scored for semantic correctness, quantitative consistency and judged reasoning quality; extends the cited APBench line in aerospace with simulation-derived instances.

title: Benchmarking AI prompt performance of large language models across chemical process systems engineering domains using multi-judge evaluation
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - PSE-Bench: 200 open-ended process-systems-engineering questions scored by a five-judge LLM ensemble against 7-element rubrics, with human validation reporting a +0.85 (0-7 scale) judge leniency bias; a chemical-engineering datapoint for the judge-validity paragraph (details from the abstract snippet; full text blocked).

title: PE Civil Bench: Advancing Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation Performance of Large Language Models on Exam Problems and Automated Component Design
notes: engineering_web: should-cite - FE and PE Civil examination questions as a standardized civil-engineering reasoning benchmark for frontier and open-weight LLMs, plus a self-correcting agentic design pipeline; the current professional-licensure-exam reference (details from the abstract snippet; full text blocked).

title: FEM-Bench: A Structured Scientific Reasoning Benchmark for Evaluating Code-Generating LLMs
notes: engineering_web: optional - graduate-level finite-element coding tasks checked by execution (33 tasks, five runs each); an execution-verified computational-mechanics benchmark adjacent to FEABench.

title: CircuitReason-1k: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Visual-to-Symbolic Reasoning in Electrical Circuits
notes: engineering_web: optional - 1,000 textbook circuit problems with reference worked solutions, scored by typed answer checks plus identity-blinded multi-model consensus; its failure analysis (topology binding, sign and phase conventions, late-stage propagation) echoes EngTrace's error analysis.

title: EngIntervene: Benchmarking Multimodal Engineering State Understanding and Design Intervention Reasoning
notes: engineering_web: optional - 3,229 questions over seven engineering domains at four levels (state grounding to design intervention), scored against structured references with atomic criteria; a late-September 2026 multi-domain benchmark between perception and design.

title: Evaluating Hydro-Science and Engineering Knowledge of Large Language Models
notes: engineering_web: optional - Hydro-SE Bench, 4,000 multiple-choice questions over nine hydraulics and water-engineering subfields (including geotechnics and hydraulic structures); covers the hydraulics branch and exemplifies the static multiple-choice format.

title: Using Large Language Models for Solving Thermodynamic Problems
notes: engineering_web: optional - 22 chemical-engineering thermodynamics problems whose LLM answers were graded by trained human experts like exam scripts; a small precedent for expert assessment of engineering solutions beyond the final number.

title: MSQA: Benchmarking LLMs on Graduate-Level Materials Science Reasoning and Knowledge
notes: engineering_web: optional - 1,757 graduate materials-science questions (explanatory and true/false) across seven sub-fields; the materials-branch reference.

title: LLMs4All: A Review of Large Language Models Across Academic Disciplines
notes: engineering_web: optional - a cross-discipline review with sections on mechanical, chemical, civil and electrical engineering; usable as the single survey pointer for LLMs in engineering.

title: VEHBench: A Stage-Local Diagnostic Benchmark for LLM-Assisted Vibration Energy Harvester Design
authors: Depeng Su, Yuyu Luo, Guobiao Hu
notes: engineering_web: optional - 763 literature-grounded vibration-energy-harvester design tasks scored by an analytical physical oracle across four design stages; a deterministic, stage-wise engineering evaluation (posted July 2026) that likewise rejects final-artifact-only scoring.

title: On the Evaluation of Engineering Artificial General Intelligence
notes: engineering_web: optional - a Bloom's-taxonomy framework for evaluating engineering AGI from methodological knowledge to real design problems, including structured artifacts (CAD, SysML); a framing citation for engineering evaluation beyond final answers.
